subject: Re: Redwood integration - SDK, auth, and key management

Subject: Redwood integration - SDK, auth, and key management (post-demo recap)

Thanks, Sophie — great conversation earlier. Quick recap and next steps so we’re aligned on scope and owners.

Recap of needs from today
- Primary use: realtime text generation + embeddings for search/reranking in customer support flows.
- Non-negotiables: data isolation, audit logs, and key rotation policy that meets your security team’s controls.
- Integration surface: backend services will call Redwood APIs (server-to-server); front-end will not hold long-lived keys.

Architecture/Integration items we discussed
1) SDK setup: we support a first-party Python/Node SDK and a raw HTTP REST API. SDK supports automatic retries, streaming, and batched embedding calls.
2) Auth options: API keys (quick), service accounts with JWT/OAuth (recommended for production), and short-lived tokens via KMS-backed signing.
3) Routing: tenant-aware routing via request headers (x-redwood-tenant-id) or dedicated model endpoints; can configure fallback to cheaper variants.
4) Structured output & tool-calling: our SDK supports structured JSON output modes and the tool-calling pattern. We can enforce output schemas server-side for safety.
5) Embeddings & rerankers: embeddings are first-class; we support hybrid dense-sparse pipelines and server-side reranking hooks.

Open questions / items for your team
- Does your infra prefer service accounts + JWTs or OAuth with your IdP?
- KMS provider and whether you need HSM-backed signing.
- Procurement timeline for enterprise contract and SOC2 evidence.

Next steps / owners
- Vivek (SE) to send integration checklist, sample code snippets for service-account auth, and an architecture diagram. (Action: Vivek, by EOD tomorrow)
- FintechCo to confirm preferred key management approach and procurement/PO timeline. (Action: Sophie/Alex)
- Marissa to coordinate a technical deep-dive (30–45m) with infra/security + legal for week of Feb 16.

Attachments: integration-checklist.xlsx (initial artifacts), redwood-sdk-auth-guide.pdf (auth patterns summary)

Thanks — happy to jump on another quick call if useful.

Thanks Marissa — that summary is super helpful. A few follow-ups from our security and infra leads before we schedule the deep dive: 

1) Can you confirm whether Redwood supports OAuth/OpenID Connect flows for server-to-server (service account) auth, or is it JWT signed by our KMS? We prefer short-lived credentials and rotating keys.
2) Do you have a recommended rotation cadence for API keys vs service-account keys?
3) For KMS integration: we use AWS KMS and have an HSM-backed key policy — can Redwood accept a signed JWT from our KMS (we'd prefer no shared long-lived secret).
4) For embeddings/rerankers: is sensitive data redaction available on ingest? We need to ensure PII is never persisted.
5) Can your SE provide a quick code sample (Node or Python) showing the SDK auth flow for a service account + JWT exchange?

If you can send answers and a short code sample, we can loop in our security lead and pick times for the week of Feb 16.

Subject: Re: Redwood integration - SDK, auth, and key management

Hi Sophie — quick technical answers and a couple of snippets. See below; attaching the SDK auth guide and an integration checklist.

Summary answers:
- OAuth/OIDC: we support standard OIDC flows for end-user auth and we also support service accounts that use JWTs signed by your KMS. For server-to-server we recommend the service-account + signed-JWT flow (no long-lived shared API key).
- KMS: Redwood accepts signed JWTs (RS256) issued by your KMS/HSM if you provide the public key. We also support an exchange endpoint where you POST a signed assertion and receive a short-lived Redwood access token (15m–1h TTL).
- Rotation cadence: for API keys we recommend rotation every 30–90 days (if used for human ops). For service-account keys signed by your KMS, rotate the signing key quarterly and use short-lived tokens (<=1h) on the client side.
- PII handling: by default, we do not persist raw inputs unless you opt into logging. We provide configurable redaction hooks at client send time (SDK) and server-side ingestion policies. We can enable automatic PII scrub for the support dataset you mentioned.

Sample flows (condensed)
1) Service-account signed-JWT exchange (curl)
POST /v1/auth/token-exchange
Headers: Content-Type: application/json
Body: {"assertion":"<signed-jwt>"}
Response: {"access_token":"ey...","expires_in":3600}

2) Python SDK (service-account)
from redwood import RedwoodClient
client = RedwoodClient.from_service_account_signed_jwt(signed_jwt='<signed-jwt-contents>')
resp = client.generate.text("Summarize customer support ticket")

Notes on public-key setup
- You can either upload a rotating JWKS to our tenant config, or we fetch your JWKS URL. Rotations are supported via key-id (kid) header.

Attachments included:
- redwood-sdk-auth-guide.pdf (detailed flows + code samples)
- integration-checklist.xlsx (what we’ll need to provision a dedicated endpoint)

Links:
- Architecture notes: https://docs.google.com/document/d/1abcdefg-integration-notes
- HubSpot deal: https://app.hubspot.com/deal/1234567890

If you want, we can add a one-hour workshop for infra/security to walk through the public-key exchange and token lifecycle.
